title: Aggregation pipelines
idea: An aggregation pipeline is an ordered list of stages. Each stage receives the documents the previous stage produced and hands its own result to the next.

analogy.text: A factory line. Raw parts enter, each station filters or reshapes them, and the finished product leaves at the end.
analogy.breaks: Your collection is not consumed: a normal pipeline only reads it.

points: A stage is an object with one operator key, such as `$match` or `$sort`.
Order matters: a `$match` after `$group` filters groups, not orders.
MongoDB runs the whole pipeline on the server and returns only the final documents.
`aggregate()` returns plain objects, not Mongoose documents, so no `.save()`.

steps.caption: The pipeline reads the `orders` collection. Every document enters the first stage.
Only paid orders reach `$group`, which builds one document per city.
`$group` emits its documents in no promised order. `$sort` fixes that.
The sorted result goes back to your Node code, one document per city.

code.title: Your first pipeline
code.caption: Step through it, then press Run for the real output from MongoDB.

walk.text: Connect, then fill `orders` and `customers`: the dataset every page of this chapter uses.
A model supplies the collection. An empty, loose schema is enough here.
The array of stages is the whole pipeline. `aggregate` returns a promise of results.
Stage 2 sums `total` per city. The next page explains `$group`.
Stage 3 sorts the cities by name.
Print the result, then disconnect so the process exits.

code.title: The shared data
code.caption: One of the 8 `orders` and one of the 5 `customers`. Here `total` is the sum of `qty * price`.

pitfalls: Add `$sort` when order matters: MongoDB promises no output order without it.
Mongoose casts `find()` filters but not pipelines: convert strings from `req.query` yourself.
Debug by running one stage first, printing it, then adding the next.

quiz.why: `$match` leaves one pending order (Cleo, Porto), so `$group` builds a single city bucket.

takeaway: A pipeline is stages in order; each one feeds the next.
